- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.2) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid overcorrection after sharp price drops — forecast should not fall below 10% below recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment is rising and price is falling, anticipate a rebound — forecast next period should be 1–3% higher than current.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers — cap forecast at ±15% of 14-day moving average to prevent overshoot.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), smooth forecast by averaging last 3 periods — reduce noise amplification.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast, adjust downward bias by 3–5% for next period — especially if sentiment is neutral or declining.
